nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Co(OH)F/CC
nodes.procedure: cobaltous nitrate hexahydrate (291 mg), urea (300 mg), and ammonium fluoride (94 mg) were dissolved in 20 mL of H2O. Then the solution was transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave (50 mL) and a piece of CC (4 × 2 cm). The autoclave was sealed and kept in an oven at 120°C for 6 h. Cooling, taking out, washing, and vacuum drying was performed to obtain the target sample.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of Co(OH)F / CC . In a typical preparation of Co(OH)F / CC , cobaltous nitrate hexahydrate (291 mg), urea (300 mg), and ammonium fluoride (94 mg) were dissolved in 20 mL of H2O . Then the solution was transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave (50 mL) and a piece of CC (4 × 2 cm). The autoclave was sealed and kept in an oven at 120°C for 6 h.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Co1-xS on Co(OH)F/CC
nodes.procedure: A typical electrodeposition electrolyte is a 0.02 M CoCl2 + 0.2 M Na2S2O3 (10 mL) solution. The deposition was carried out by chronopotentiometry with a three-electrode system, the working electrode was Co(OH)F/CC, the reference electrode was Ag/AgCl electrode, and the counter electrode was a graphite rod. In the electrolyte at 70°C, the cathodic current was set to 0.004 A (2 mAcm^{-2}) with a cathodic time of 480 s. Taking out, clearing, and drying was performed to obtain the target product.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show needle-like nanowire structure of Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F/CC with average diameter 150-200 nm and rougher surface compared to Co(OH)F/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with Co(OH)F/CC, Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F/CC still retains the uniform nanowire structure, and the average diameter distribution of Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F/CC is about 150-200 nm (Figure 1b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms Co_{1-x}S nanoparticles with diameter 5-6 nm on Co(OH)F nanowires.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image results also confirmed the existence of Co_{1-x}S nanoparticles with a diameter of about 5-6 nm (inset Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.18 nm and 0.25 nm for (221) and (111) planes of Co(OH)F, and 0.29 nm for (100) plane of Co_{1-x}S, with Co_{1-x}S growing along Co(OH)F defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1e-g, the lattice fringes of 0.18 and 0.25 nm are attributed to the (221) and (111) planes of Co(OH)F, respectively, and the lattice spacing of 0.29 nm corresponds to the (100) plane of Co_{1-x}S.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX element mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Co, O, F, and S elements in Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F nanowire.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping results (Figure 1h) show the homogeneous distribution of Co, O, F, and S elements in the Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F nanowire.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD peaks indexed to Co(OH)F (PDF: 50-0827) with positive shift in Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F/CC compared to Co(OH)F/CC, indicating strong electronic interaction; Co_{1-x}S signal not detected due to small size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All diffraction peaks except for the peak of CC could be well indexed to Co(OH)F (PDF: 50-0827). Obviously, due to the low content of Co_{1-x}S nanoparticles with small size (≤6 nm), the corresponding signal could not be detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Co(OH)F characteristic peaks at 481.2, 508.3, 663.3 cm^{-1} blue-shifted in Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F due to Co-S-Co bond formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic peaks of Co(OH)F were obviously observed at the displacement of 481.2, 508.3, and 663.3 cm^{-1}. Compared with Co(OH)F, the three characteristic peaks of Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F are blue-shifted...

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS of Co 2p shows Co^{2+} peaks at 797.7 eV (2p_{1/2}) and 782.7 eV (2p_{3/2}), Co^{3+} at 796.5 eV (2p_{1/2}) and 780.6 eV (2p_{3/2}, Co-S bond); S 2p shows 163.4/164.4 eV (S 2p_{3/2}/2p_{1/2}) and 161.6/162.5 eV (Co-S); negative shifts indicate strong electronic interaction between Co_{1-x}S and Co(OH)F.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1j, the high-resolution Co 2p of the XPS spectrum, the peaks at around 797.7 and 782.7 eV can be assigned to Co^{2+}2p_{1/2} and Co^{2+}2p_{3/2}, respectively. The peaks at around 796.5 and 780.6 eV can be assigned to Co^{3+}2p_{1/2} and Co^{3+}2p_{3/2}, respectively... In Figure 1k, the high-resolution S 2p spectra, the two peaks centered at 163.4 and 164.4 eV could be ascribed to S 2p_{3/2} and S 2p_{1/2}.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES of Co(OH)F-S shows absorption edge between Co(OH)F and CoO with leftward shift, indicating valence change of Co atoms upon S introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In XANES, the absorption edge of Co(OH)F-S is located between Co(OH)F and CoO. Compared with Co(OH)F, Co(OH)F-S shows a similar near-edge structure, but the curve moves slightly to the left...

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Co-Co at 2.17 Å, Co-O at 1.7 Å, Co-O/F at 1.62 Å, Co-S at 1.91 Å in Co(OH)F-S; Co-F and Co-O peaks show red shift due to S replacing F atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2e shows the Fourier transform (FT) k^3-weighted extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectral data... The Co-Co, Co-O, Co-O/F, and Co-S coordination peaks are detected at 2.17, 1.7, 1.62, and 1.91 Å, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl = 181.3 mF cm^{-2} for Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F/CC (vs 141.2 mF cm^{-2} for Co(OH)F/CC), indicating higher density of active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3e, the C_dl of electrodes Co_{1-x}S/Co(OH)F/CC, Co(OH)F/CC, and Co_{1-x}S/CC were 181.3, 141.2, and 86.5 mF cm^{-2}, respectively...
